Class Queries

java.lang.Object
edu.tamu.project2.csce331.Queries
public class Queries extends Object
Data-access facade for the POS application.

Provides read/write operations over the core schema: personnel, menu, seasonal_menu, ingredients, ingredients_map, transactions, and transaction_details. Methods use JDBC (try-with-resources), acquire connections via Database.getConnection(), and throw SQLException on database errors.

Organization:

  • EMPLOYEES – get/add/update/delete/count employees
  • MENU and ITEMS – menu fetch, item lookups, item–ingredient mapping, CRUD
  • SEASONAL MENU – seasonal menu fetch/add/delete
  • INGREDIENTS – ingredient CRUD, inventory adjustments, lookups
  • TRANSACTIONS – list/count/get transactions, add with details
  • HELPERS – private utilities used by other methods

Notes:

  • Queries target a PostgreSQL schema and rely on the defined foreign keys/indexes.
  • Transactional boundaries are caller-controlled unless otherwise documented.
  • Return types favor order-preserving collections (e.g., LinkedHashMap) when SQL specifies ordering.
Author:
Daniel Zhang, Brendan Larson

      public ArrayList<Employee> get_managers() throws SQLException
      Retrieves all active employees whose role is 'manager' from the personnel table.

      This method executes a simple SELECT filtered on role = 'manager' and constructs Employee instances for each matching row. The list preserves the database iteration order.

    • update_seasonal_price

      public void update_seasonal_price(int id, double price) throws SQLException
      Updates the price of a seasonal menu item.

      Executes the SQL statement UPDATE seasonal_menu SET price = ? WHERE item_id = ? using a PreparedStatement obtained from Database.getConnection(). Resources are managed via try-with-resources.

      Parameters:
      id - the identifier of the seasonal menu item to update
      price - the new price to set for the item
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs while preparing or executing the update

      Note: this method does not currently verify the number of affected rows; if item_id does not exist, the call completes without error but no data is changed.

    • get_ingredient_usage

      public ArrayList<IngredientUsage> get_ingredient_usage(Timestamp start, Timestamp end) throws SQLException
      Retrieves a mapping of ingredient names to the number of times each ingredient was used in transactions within a specified time range.

      This method queries the database by joining the transactions, transaction_details, ingredients_map, and ingredients tables. Each transaction within the given timestamp range contributes counts for its associated ingredients. The results are ordered by usage frequency (descending) and ingredient name, and returned as a LinkedHashMap to preserve that order.

      Parameters:
      start - the inclusive lower bound of the timestamp range
      end - the inclusive upper bound of the timestamp range
      Returns:
      a map where each key is an ingredient name and each value is the number of times that ingredient was used during the period
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

    • get_sales_report

      public ArrayList<TimeItemName> get_sales_report(Timestamp start, Timestamp end) throws SQLException
      Produces a reverse-chronological “sales tape” of items sold within a time window.

      Each row in the result represents one sold item (one row in transaction_details), joined to its transaction timestamp and menu name. Results are ordered by transactions.transaction_time descending, then menu.item_name ascending for stable per-timestamp ordering.

      Parameters:
      start - inclusive lower bound for transactions.transaction_time
      end - inclusive upper bound for transactions.transaction_time
      Returns:
      a list of TimeItemName pairs, one per item sold in the window
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs

      Notes:

      • Assumes transaction_details(transaction_id) and menu(item_id) foreign keys.
      • For large ranges, consider paging (LIMIT/OFFSET) or streaming the ResultSet.
      • Indexes on transactions(transaction_time), transaction_details(transaction_id), and transaction_details(item_id) will improve performance.

    • add_transaction_and_details

      public void add_transaction_and_details(Transaction transaction, ArrayList<Item> items) throws SQLException
      Inserts a transaction header and its associated item detail rows atomically.

      This method begins a transaction, creates the transactions row, then inserts corresponding transaction_details rows for each provided item. All changes are committed together or rolled back on failure.

      Parameters:
      transaction - the transaction header data (customer, time, employee, total)
      items - the list of items sold in the transaction
      Throws:
      SQLException - if any database operation fails
